The KJV wording: "Joseph, which was the son of Heli" (Lk 3:23). Default reading: it follows the text and nothing else. Mt 1:16 says "Jacob begat Joseph". See case heli_lk3_23.
Alternative reading: Joseph is Jacob's son by nature (Mt 1:16) and Heli's by law, Jacob having raised up seed to Heli who died childless (Deut 25:5-6).
Alternative reading (not the KJV wording): Luke traces Mary's line; Heli is Mary's father and Joseph his son-in-law. TIPNR follows this reading. The text never names Mary's father.
Raised from derived to certain: stated in Matthew 1: Abraham to Jesus (Mat 1:2).. BibleData: inferred GEN 25:26; inferred GEN 25:26
"Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary" (Mt 1:16).
Pedaiah is listed under "the sons of Jeconiah; Assir, Salathiel his son, Malchiram also, and Pedaiah ..." (1 Chr 3:17-18). TIPNR instead makes him a son of Shealtiel (?).
"Joram begat Ozias" (Mt 1:8): Ozias (Uzziah/Azariah) is Joram's great-great-grandson through Ahaziah, Joash and Amaziah (1 Chr 3:11-12).

"Josias begat Jechonias and his brethren" (Mt 1:11): Jeconiah is Josiah's grandson through Jehoiakim (1 Chr 3:15-16).

sources.name: STEPBible TIPNR (Translators Individualised Proper Names with all References)
sources.attribution: Data created by www.STEPBible.org based on work at Tyndale House Cambridge (CC BY 4.0).
sources.notes: TIPNR asks users to reformat "without changing the data", to publish a note of changes, and "please do not redistribute it yourself" (refer others to github.com/STEPBible). CHANGE LOG (what this dataset does to TIPNR): (1) reformatted into person / relationship rows with slug ids; the TIPNR unique name is kept in person_external_id (scheme tipnr); (2) display names are the KJV form of each name (TIPNR uses the ESV form; the ESV/NIV forms are kept as aliases); (3) persons TIPNR infers but the text never names are left out with their links (e.g. wife_of_Heli, father_of_Elizabeth, and Unnamed#1-9@Mat.1.15 which TIPNR inserts between Matthan and Jacob where the KJV says "Matthan begat Jacob"); (4) links for which no verse names both persons are left out (listed in the conflict report); (5) where the KJV text states a link differently, the KJV wording is the default and TIPNR's choice is kept as an alternative reading: Heli is the father of Joseph by the wording of Lk 3:23 (TIPNR: of Mary), Arphaxad begat Salah (Gen 11:12; TIPNR: Cainan only), Salathiel begat Zorobabel (Mt 1:12; TIPNR: Pedaiah only); (6) Mary's tribe is left empty (TIPNR: Levi); (7) TIPNR "(?)" links are rated possible, "(a)"/"(d)" parents become qualifier ancestor, "(d)"/"(f)" of a group become founded_by. Proposed corrections should be sent to STEPBible rather than distributed from here.

cases.title: Joseph "the son of Heli" (Luke 3:23) and "Jacob begat Joseph" (Matthew 1:16)
cases.text: Luk 3:23 "And Jesus himself began to be about thirty years of age, being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph, which was the son of Heli," Mat 1:16 "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."

readings.label: default
readings.summary: The KJV wording as it stands: Joseph was "the son of Heli" (Lk 3:23) and "Jacob begat Joseph" (Mt 1:16). The dataset shows the Heli link with this wording as its default reading, beside Jacob.

readings.label: heli_father_of_mary
readings.summary: Luke gives Mary's line: Heli was Mary's father and Joseph is called his son as his son-in-law (or stands in Mary's place in the list).
readings.heldBy: Annius of Viterbo (c. 1490) and many later Protestant commentators; followed by TIPNR

readings.label: levirate_or_legal
readings.summary: Jacob and Heli were brothers by the same mother; Heli died childless and Jacob raised up seed to him (Deut 25:5-6), so Joseph was Jacob's son by nature and Heli's by law.
readings.heldBy: Julius Africanus, Letter to Aristides (3rd century, in Eusebius, Church History 1.7)

cases.title: Jesus "as was supposed" the son of Joseph
cases.text: Luk 3:23 "And Jesus himself began to be about thirty years of age, being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph, which was the son of Heli," Mat 1:16 "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ." Mat 1:18 "Now the birth of Jesus Christ was on this wise: When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost." Mat 1:20 "But while he thought on these things, behold, the angel of the Lord appeared unto him in a dream, saying, Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." Mat 1:25 "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS." Luk 1:34 "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" Luk 1:35 "And the angel answered and said unto her, The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."

readings.label: legal_father
readings.summary: Jesus was conceived of the Holy Ghost and born of Mary; Joseph, her husband, was his father in law and in the eyes of men ("as was supposed"). Modelled as father_of with qualifier legal; Mary as mother_of.

cases.title: "Joram begat Ozias": three kings not named (Matthew 1:8)
cases.text: Mat 1:8 "And Asa begat Josaphat; and Josaphat begat Joram; and Joram begat Ozias;" 1Ch 3:11 "Joram his son, Ahaziah his son, Joash his son," 1Ch 3:12 "Amaziah his son, Azariah his son, Jotham his son,"

readings.label: begat_as_forefather
readings.summary: "Begat" here means "was the forefather of": Matthew abridges the list to make three sets of fourteen (Mt 1:17). Modelled as father_of with qualifier ancestor and a gap before Ozias.

readings.label: omission_for_ahab_line
readings.summary: Ahaziah, Joash and Amaziah were left out because they descended from Ahab through Athaliah (2 Ki 8:18, 26), under the judgment "unto the third and fourth generation" (Ex 20:5).

cases.title: "Josias begat Jechonias": Jehoiakim not named (Matthew 1:11)
cases.text: Mat 1:11 "And Josias begat Jechonias and his brethren, about the time they were carried away to Babylon:" 1Ch 3:15 "And the sons of Josiah were, the firstborn Johanan, the second Jehoiakim, the third Zedekiah, the fourth Shallum." 1Ch 3:16 "And the sons of Jehoiakim: Jeconiah his son, Zedekiah his son."

readings.label: begat_as_forefather
readings.summary: Josiah was Jechonias' grandfather through Jehoiakim; "begat" means "was the forefather of". Modelled as father_of with qualifier ancestor and a gap before Jechonias.

readings.label: brethren_as_generation
readings.summary: "Jechonias and his brethren" takes in the generation of Josiah's sons, of whom Jehoiakim was one.

cases.title: Three sets of fourteen generations (Matthew 1:17)
cases.text: Mat 1:17 "So all the generations from Abraham to David are fourteen generations; and from David until the carrying away into Babylon are fourteen generations; and from the carrying away into Babylon unto Christ are fourteen generations."

readings.label: shared_endpoints
readings.summary: The sets are counted with a person closing one set and opening the next (David, or Jechonias), so the third set reaches fourteen with Jesus.

readings.label: arrangement
readings.summary: The count is an arrangement for remembrance, made possible by the names Matthew leaves out (Mt 1:8, 11).

cases.title: "Son" and "begat" for a descendant
cases.text: Mat 1:1 "The book of the generation of Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham." Mat 1:8 "And Asa begat Josaphat; and Josaphat begat Joram; and Joram begat Ozias;"

readings.label: descendant
readings.summary: "The son of David, the son of Abraham" (Mt 1:1) calls a descendant a son; the same use of "begat" (Mt 1:8, 11) lets a genealogy pass over generations. The dataset models such links as father_of with qualifier ancestor, never as a plain parent link.

cases.title: Cainan between Sala and Arphaxad (Luke 3:36)
cases.text: Luk 3:35 "Which was the son of Saruch, which was the son of Ragau, which was the son of Phalec, which was the son of Heber, which was the son of Sala," Luk 3:36 "Which was the son of Cainan, which was the son of Arphaxad, which was the son of Sem, which was the son of Noe, which was the son of Lamech," Gen 11:12 "And Arphaxad lived five and thirty years, and begat Salah:" 1Ch 1:18 "And Arphaxad begat Shelah, and Shelah begat Eber." 1Ch 1:24 "Shem, Arphaxad, Shelah,"

readings.label: genesis_abridged
readings.summary: Both texts stand: Luke names a generation that Genesis 11 and 1 Chronicles 1 pass over, "begat" in Genesis 11:12 meaning "was the forefather of". The dataset keeps both links (Arphaxad father_of Salah; Arphaxad father_of Cainan father_of Sala) and marks Cainan "Luke only".
readings.heldBy: Commentators who hold both texts exact

readings.label: septuagint
readings.summary: Luke follows the Greek Septuagint of Genesis 11:12-13 and 10:24, which has Cainan between Arphaxad and Salah.

readings.label: scribal_addition
readings.summary: Cainan in Luke 3:36 entered the text of Luke from the Septuagint in early copying.

cases.title: Zerubbabel "the son of Shealtiel" and "the sons of Pedaiah"
cases.text: Mat 1:12 "And after they were brought to Babylon, Jechonias begat Salathiel; and Salathiel begat Zorobabel;" Ezr 3:2 "Then stood up Jeshua the son of Jozadak, and his brethren the priests, and Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and his brethren, and builded the altar of the God of Israel, to offer burnt offerings thereon, as it is written in the law of Moses the man of God." Hag 1:1 "In the second year of Darius the king, in the sixth month, in the first day of the month, came the word of the LORD by Haggai the prophet unto Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and to Joshua the son of Josedech, the high priest, saying," 1Ch 3:17 "And the sons of Jeconiah; Assir, Salathiel his son," 1Ch 3:18 "Malchiram also, and Pedaiah, and Shenazar, Jecamiah, Hoshama, and Nedabiah." 1Ch 3:19 "And the sons of Pedaiah were, Zerubbabel, and Shimei: and the sons of Zerubbabel; Meshullam, and Hananiah, and Shelomith their sister:" [Dataset: The dataset keeps both links as the text states them: Salathiel father_of Zorobabel (Mt 1:12) and Pedaiah father_of Zerubbabel (1 Chr 3:19).]

readings.label: levirate
readings.summary: Shealtiel died without a son; his brother Pedaiah raised up seed to him (Deut 25:5-6), so Zerubbabel was Pedaiah's son by nature and Shealtiel's by law.

readings.label: grandson_or_heir
readings.summary: Zerubbabel was Pedaiah's son and Shealtiel's grandson or legal heir; "son of Shealtiel" names the head of the line.

readings.label: two_zerubbabels
readings.summary: The Zerubbabel of 1 Chronicles 3:19 is a different man from the governor of Ezra and Haggai.

cases.title: Salathiel and Zorobabel in both genealogies (Matthew 1:12, Luke 3:27)
cases.text: Mat 1:12 "And after they were brought to Babylon, Jechonias begat Salathiel; and Salathiel begat Zorobabel;" Luk 3:27 "Which was the son of Joanna, which was the son of Rhesa, which was the son of Zorobabel, which was the son of Salathiel, which was the son of Neri,"

readings.label: different_persons
readings.summary: Namesakes: Luke's Salathiel son of Neri and Zorobabel father of Rhesa are other men than Matthew's. The dataset keeps them apart (as TIPNR does) and links them as possibly_same_as.

readings.label: same_persons
readings.summary: The same two men: Salathiel was Jechonias' son by nature and Neri's by law or by marriage (or the reverse), the two lines meeting here.

cases.title: "Write ye this man childless" (Jeremiah 22:30) and "Jechonias begat Salathiel"
cases.text: Jer 22:30 "Thus saith the LORD, Write ye this man childless, a man that shall not prosper in his days: for no man of his seed shall prosper, sitting upon the throne of David, and ruling any more in Judah." Mat 1:12 "And after they were brought to Babylon, Jechonias begat Salathiel; and Salathiel begat Zorobabel;" 1Ch 3:17 "And the sons of Jeconiah; Assir, Salathiel his son,"

readings.label: throne_not_seed
readings.summary: "Childless" is explained by what follows: "no man of his seed shall prosper, sitting upon the throne of David". Jeconiah had sons (1 Chr 3:17), but none reigned; Jesus is Joseph's son by law, not Jeconiah's seed by nature.

readings.label: judgment_reversed
readings.summary: The sentence was reversed for his grandson: "I will take thee, O Zerubbabel ... and will make thee as a signet" (Hag 2:23), answering Jer 22:24.

cases.title: Ozias, Uzziah and Azariah: one king
cases.text: Mat 1:8 "And Asa begat Josaphat; and Josaphat begat Joram; and Joram begat Ozias;" 2Ki 15:1 "In the twenty and seventh year of Jeroboam king of Israel began Azariah son of Amaziah king of Judah to reign." 2Ki 15:13 "Shallum the son of Jabesh began to reign in the nine and thirtieth year of Uzziah king of Judah; and he reigned a full month in Samaria." 1Ch 3:12 "Amaziah his son, Azariah his son, Jotham his son,"

readings.label: one_person
readings.summary: Azariah (2 Ki 15:1; 1 Chr 3:12) and Uzziah (2 Ki 15:13; 2 Chr 26:1) are two names of one king, called Ozias in Mt 1:8-9. One person with aliases.

cases.title: Jehoiachin, Jeconiah, Coniah and Jechonias: one king
cases.text: 2Ki 24:6 "So Jehoiakim slept with his fathers: and Jehoiachin his son reigned in his stead." 1Ch 3:16 "And the sons of Jehoiakim: Jeconiah his son, Zedekiah his son." Jer 22:24 "As I live, saith the LORD, though Coniah the son of Jehoiakim king of Judah were the signet upon my right hand, yet would I pluck thee thence;" Mat 1:11 "And Josias begat Jechonias and his brethren, about the time they were carried away to Babylon:"

readings.label: one_person
readings.summary: Jehoiachin (2 Ki 24:6), Jeconiah (1 Chr 3:16), Coniah (Jer 22:24) and Jechonias (Mt 1:11-12) are one king. One person with aliases.

cases.title: Mary's tribe
cases.text: Luk 1:27 "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David; and the virgin’s name was Mary." Luk 1:32 "He shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David:" Luk 1:36 "And, behold, thy cousin Elisabeth, she hath also conceived a son in her old age: and this is the sixth month with her, who was called barren." Luk 1:5 "There was in the days of Herod, the king of Judæa, a certain priest named Zacharias, of the course of Abia: and his wife was of the daughters of Aaron, and her name was Elisabeth." Rom 1:3 "Concerning his Son Jesus Christ our Lord, which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh;"

readings.label: unstated
readings.summary: The text names no tribe for Mary. The dataset leaves it empty.

readings.label: judah_david
readings.summary: Mary was of David's house: Jesus "was made of the seed of David according to the flesh" (Rom 1:3) and "sprang out of Juda" (Heb 7:14).

readings.label: levi
readings.summary: Mary was of Levi, being Elisabeth's cousin (Lk 1:36), and Elisabeth "of the daughters of Aaron" (Lk 1:5).

cases.title: Rachab the mother of Booz (Matthew 1:5) and Rahab of Jericho
cases.text: Mat 1:5 "And Salmon begat Booz of Rachab; and Booz begat Obed of Ruth; and Obed begat Jesse;" Jos 6:25 "And Joshua saved Rahab the harlot alive, and her father’s household, and all that she had; and she dwelleth in Israel even unto this day; because she hid the messengers, which Joshua sent to spy out Jericho." Heb 11:31 "By faith the harlot Rahab perished not with them that believed not, when she had received the spies with peace."

readings.label: same_woman
readings.summary: Rachab is Rahab of Jericho, who "dwelleth in Israel" (Jos 6:25) and married Salmon.

readings.label: unstated
readings.summary: The text does not say that Salmon's wife was the Rahab of Jericho; the identification is an inference.

cases.title: Obed: "a son born to Naomi" and the name of the dead (Ruth 4)
cases.text: Rut 4:10 "Moreover Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of Mahlon, have I purchased to be my wife, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance, that the name of the dead be not cut off from among his brethren, and from the gate of his place: ye are witnesses this day." Rut 4:13 "So Boaz took Ruth, and she was his wife: and when he went in unto her, the LORD gave her conception, and she bare a son." Rut 4:17 "And the women her neighbours gave it a name, saying, There is a son born to Naomi; and they called his name Obed: he is the father of Jesse, the father of David." Rut 4:21 "And Salmon begat Boaz, and Boaz begat Obed,"

readings.label: boaz_father
readings.summary: "Boaz begat Obed" (Ruth 4:21; Mt 1:5): Boaz is his father and the genealogies count him so. Modelled as father_of without qualifier.

readings.label: heir_of_mahlon
readings.summary: Boaz married Ruth "to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance" (4:10), so Obed was also reckoned the heir of Mahlon and Elimelech ("a son born to Naomi", 4:17). Not modelled as a link; noted here.

cases.title: Salmon to David in four generations (Ruth 4:20-22)
cases.text: Rut 4:20 "And Amminadab begat Nahshon, and Nahshon begat Salmon," Rut 4:21 "And Salmon begat Boaz, and Boaz begat Obed," Rut 4:22 "And Obed begat Jesse, and Jesse begat David." 1Ki 6:1 "And it came to pass in the four hundred and eightieth year after the children of Israel were come out of the land of Egypt, in the fourth year of Solomon’s reign over Israel, in the month Zif, which is the second month, that he began to build the house of the LORD." [Dataset: The dataset models every link as the text states it (father_of), without inferred gaps.]

readings.label: complete
readings.summary: The list is complete: each "begat" is father to son, the men being long-lived or old at the birth of their sons.

readings.label: abridged
readings.summary: The list passes over generations between Salmon and David ("begat" as "was the forefather of"), given the span of the judges (1 Ki 6:1).

cases.title: Levi, Kohath, Amram, Moses: four generations for the sojourn (Exodus 6)
cases.text: Exo 6:16 "And these are the names of the sons of Levi according to their generations; Gershon, and Kohath, and Merari: and the years of the life of Levi were an hundred thirty and seven years." Exo 6:18 "And the sons of Kohath; Amram, and Izhar, and Hebron, and Uzziel: and the years of the life of Kohath were an hundred thirty and three years." Exo 6:20 "And Amram took him Jochebed his father’s sister to wife; and she bare him Aaron and Moses: and the years of the life of Amram were an hundred and thirty and seven years." Exo 12:40 "Now the sojourning of the children of Israel, who dwelt in Egypt, was four hundred and thirty years." Num 3:27 "And of Kohath was the family of the Amramites, and the family of the Izeharites, and the family of the Hebronites, and the family of the Uzzielites: these are the families of the Kohathites." Num 3:28 "In the number of all the males, from a month old and upward, were eight thousand and six hundred, keeping the charge of the sanctuary." [Dataset: Modelled as the text states it: Amram father_of Aaron and Moses (Ex 6:20).]

readings.label: immediate
readings.summary: Amram and Jochebed were Moses' father and mother, Jochebed being "the daughter of Levi" (Num 26:59); the sojourn is covered by the long lives given in Exodus 6.

readings.label: ancestor
readings.summary: The Amram of Exodus 6:18 is the head of the Amramites, and Moses' father (of the same name, or unnamed in Ex 2:1) came generations later, given the Kohathites' number in Moses' day (Num 3:27-28).

cases.title: Kish "the son of Abiel" and "Ner begat Kish"
cases.text: 1Sa 9:1 "Now there was a man of Benjamin, whose name was Kish, the son of Abiel, the son of Zeror, the son of Bechorath, the son of Aphiah, a Benjamite, a mighty man of power." 1Sa 14:51 "And Kish was the father of Saul; and Ner the father of Abner was the son of Abiel." 1Ch 8:33 "And Ner begat Kish, and Kish begat Saul, and Saul begat Jonathan, and Malchi-shua, and Abinadab, and Esh-baal." 1Ch 9:39 "And Ner begat Kish; and Kish begat Saul; and Saul begat Jonathan, and Malchi-shua, and Abinadab, and Esh-baal." [Dataset: Imported as TIPNR has it (Abiel father_of Kish); the "Ner begat Kish" link is listed in the conflict report for review.]

readings.label: two_kishes_or_ancestor
readings.summary: 1 Chr 9:36 has an elder Kish, brother of Ner; Ner "begat Kish" (1 Chr 8:33; 9:39) and Abiel is named as a forefather, or as another name. The text names both Abiel (1 Sam 9:1) and Ner as Kish's father.

readings.label: abiel_father
readings.summary: Kish and Ner were both sons of Abiel (1 Sam 14:51); "Ner begat Kish" in Chronicles names Ner as the head of the house.

cases.title: "Terah ... begat Abram, Nahor, and Haran": birth order
cases.text: Gen 11:26 "And Terah lived seventy years, and begat Abram, Nahor, and Haran." Gen 11:32 "And the days of Terah were two hundred and five years: and Terah died in Haran." Gen 12:4 "So Abram departed, as the LORD had spoken unto him; and Lot went with him: and Abram was seventy and five years old when he departed out of Haran." Act 7:4 "Then came he out of the land of the Chaldæans, and dwelt in Charran: and from thence, when his father was dead, he removed him into this land, wherein ye now dwell." [Dataset: No sort_order is set for Terah's sons.]

readings.label: abram_first_named
readings.summary: Abram is named first for his importance; he was born when Terah was 130, since Terah died at 205 (Gen 11:32) and Abram left Haran at 75 after his father's death (Gen 12:4; Acts 7:4).

readings.label: abram_eldest
readings.summary: Abram was the eldest, born in Terah's seventieth year; Acts 7:4 is read otherwise.

cases.title: "Shem also, the father of all the children of Eber, the brother of Japheth the elder"
cases.text: Gen 10:21 "Unto Shem also, the father of all the children of Eber, the brother of Japheth the elder, even to him were children born." Gen 5:32 "And Noah was five hundred years old: and Noah begat Shem, Ham, and Japheth." Gen 9:24 "And Noah awoke from his wine, and knew what his younger son had done unto him." [Dataset: No sort_order is set for Noah's sons.]

readings.label: japheth_elder
readings.summary: The KJV wording: Japheth is "the elder"; Shem is named first for the promise.

readings.label: shem_elder
readings.summary: The Hebrew can be read "Shem ... the elder brother of Japheth".

cases.title: The names of Esau's wives (Genesis 26, 28 and 36)
cases.text: Gen 26:34 "And Esau was forty years old when he took to wife Judith the daughter of Beeri the Hittite, and Bashemath the daughter of Elon the Hittite:" Gen 28:9 "Then went Esau unto Ishmael, and took unto the wives which he had Mahalath the daughter of Ishmael Abraham’s son, the sister of Nebajoth, to be his wife." Gen 36:2 "Esau took his wives of the daughters of Canaan; Adah the daughter of Elon the Hittite, and Aholibamah the daughter of Anah the daughter of Zibeon the Hivite;" Gen 36:3 "And Bashemath Ishmael’s daughter, sister of Nebajoth." [Dataset: Imported as TIPNR identifies them; the identifications are for review.]

readings.label: second_names
readings.summary: The wives bore more than one name: Bashemath daughter of Elon (26:34) is Adah (36:2), and Mahalath daughter of Ishmael (28:9) is Bashemath (36:3).

cases.title: Reuel, Raguel, Jethro and Hobab
cases.text: Exo 2:18 "And when they came to Reuel their father, he said, How is it that ye are come so soon to day?" Exo 3:1 "Now Moses kept the flock of Jethro his father in law, the priest of Midian: and he led the flock to the backside of the desert, and came to the mountain of God, even to Horeb." Num 10:29 "And Moses said unto Hobab, the son of Raguel the Midianite, Moses’ father in law, We are journeying unto the place of which the LORD said, I will give it you: come thou with us, and we will do thee good: for the LORD hath spoken good concerning Israel." Jdg 4:11 "Now Heber the Kenite, which was of the children of Hobab the father in law of Moses, had severed himself from the Kenites, and pitched his tent unto the plain of Zaanaim, which is by Kedesh."

readings.label: jethro_reuel_one
readings.summary: Reuel (Raguel) and Jethro are one man, Moses' father-in-law; Hobab is his son (Num 10:29).

readings.label: reuel_grandfather
readings.summary: Reuel was the girls' grandfather ("their father", Ex 2:18); Jethro, and in Judges 4:11 Hobab, is the father-in-law.

cases.title: Ages in Genesis 5 and 11 are not modelled
cases.text: Gen 5:3 "And Adam lived an hundred and thirty years, and begat a son in his own likeness, after his image; and called his name Seth:" Gen 11:10 "These are the generations of Shem: Shem was an hundred years old, and begat Arphaxad two years after the flood:"

readings.label: out_of_scope
readings.summary: The ages at begetting and at death are part of the chronology (timeline module, task 0066), not of these genealogies. The lineages here record only the order and the links.
